turns.content: For Boc-Phe-Ala(3-N3)-OMe, what intermediate is produced if azide undergoes beta elimination before nucleophilic addition? Assume the L-Phe stereocenter is retained.
What geometry does that intermediate have at the alanine-derived carbon, and what happens to the original alanine stereocenter?
If the nucleophile can add from either face of that intermediate while L-Phe remains chiral, how are the two products related?
What experimental observation would most specifically support the proposed pathway, and why is it more diagnostic than a bulk physical change or simple loss of the azide group?
How strong is that evidence without structures or stereochemical assignments for the two separated products and without excluding unrelated same-mass isomers?
Name a structural or kinetic follow-up that could distinguish the proposed product pair from unrelated same-mass species and link it to the intermediate.
State the best-supported mechanistic conclusion and its main evidential limitation.
